story_name: Mr. E and the Two Impossible Machines
story_overview: An original animated story about Elias Reed, nicknamed Mr. E, a fictional silver-haired inventor with round amber glasses and a teal work jacket. During one busy day he sketches a reusable spacecraft, visits Volt Harbor, an electric vehicle company, and checks in with Aster Loop, a reusable rocket company. The tone is playful and hopeful, with stylized 3D animation, expressive character acting, and a consistent original character design. All people, companies, products, and events are fictional.

video_prompts: Original stylized 3D animated film, clearly fictional and not photorealistic. At sunrise, Elias Reed, known as Mr. E, is a lean middle-aged inventor with swept silver hair, round amber glasses, a short angular beard, and a teal work jacket over a mustard shirt. He sits at a colorful workshop kitchen island, sipping coffee and reading a translucent tablet. Warm sunlight streams through circular windows. Medium shot with a gentle camera pan, playful handcrafted textures, expressive animation, no resemblance to any real person.

In the same original stylized 3D animation, Mr. E sketches a ring-shaped reusable spacecraft on a paper napkin beside his coffee. Tiny wind-up robot toys wobble on a shelf behind him. Close-up of the drawing, then his delighted raised eyebrow; warm soft lighting and whimsical timing. Preserve his silver hair, amber glasses, angular beard, teal jacket, and mustard shirt exactly.

Mr. E notices a chiming brass wristwatch, realizes he is late, and hurriedly catches a rolling blueprint tube before grabbing his satchel. The camera follows him toward a round workshop door in a lively animated tracking shot. Comedic physical acting, bright morning colors, fully fictional character and setting.

Mr. E pauses beside an original compact electric delivery vehicle with a rounded glass canopy. He taps a removable battery panel while a young engineer demonstrates a modular connector. Medium two-shot, slow circular camera move, curious expressions and collaborative body language. Clearly fictional animated product with no badges, logos, or resemblance to a real vehicle.

The Volt Harbor team sketches notes and assembles the shapes into a tiny glowing city model. Close-up on expressive hands and faces, then a subtle push toward the model. video_prompts: At late afternoon, Mr. E visits Aster Loop, a fictional reusable rocket company built inside a seaside cliff hangar. An original short, wide spacecraft rests on articulated landing legs while engineers inspect its heat-shield tiles. Mr. E watches from a safe observation balcony with a cup of tea. Wide stylized 3D animated shot, ocean light, bold graphic shapes, no real logos or vehicle designs.

A gentle test pulse lifts the fictional spacecraft a few meters before it settles precisely onto its landing marks. Reflections dance across Mr. E's amber glasses as a breeze ruffles his swept silver hair. The animated camera tilts from his delighted profile toward the hovering craft and the evening sky. Serene wonder with playful mechanical detail.

After sunset, Mr. E stands on the hangar roof beside a small blinking service robot. He pins the morning napkin sketch to a corkboard labeled Tomorrow and quietly smiles as a reddish planet rises over the ocean. The camera slowly pulls back, framing the original fictional inventor, the distant reusable craft, and the stars. Hopeful stylized 3D animation, soft fade to black.
